caption: The video captures a polar night scene beneath a star-scattered sky, where the Milky Way band stretches across the left. Dark, jagged mountains rise along the horizon above a glassy, mirror-like water surface. A luminous green aurora hangs in the sky, its bright vertical column glowing near the center in the opening frames. As the clip progresses, this central column drifts slowly leftward, stretching and reshaping in place while the lower horizon glow behind the peak also slides left and fades a touch. In the later frames a faint secondary green patch becomes more visible on the right side of the sky. The foreground reflection tracks the moving light, its bright green mirror shifting left and breaking into smaller, dimmer fragments. The mountains, stars, and Milky Way remain fixed, so the visible motion belongs to the aurora and its reflection rather than the landscape.
relations: Central aurora column drifting leftward and stretching causes its mirror reflection to shift left and fragment.
Lower horizon glow sliding left and fading dims the corresponding reflected band on the water.
Emerging right-side green patch appears in sky without strong reflection, as mountains and stars stay fixed.
Fixed landscape ensures visible motion belongs only to aurora shapes and their water reflections.
